options.text: It helps businesses increase their profits.
It ensures consumers are treated fairly.
It allows consumers to buy more products.

questions.explanation: Consumer protection is important because it ensures that consumers are treated fairly and are not exploited by businesses. This fosters trust in the market.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect because consumer protection focuses on fairness, not just profits.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is misleading; consumer protection is about rights, not just increasing purchases.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect as consumer protection encourages healthy competition.

questions.stem: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and drug safety in Nigeria?

options.text: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

questions.explanation: NAFDAC is specifically tasked with regulating food and drug safety, ensuring that these products are safe for consumers.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect as FCCPC focuses on competition and consumer rights, not specifically food and drug safety.
distractorRationale.b: Option b is wrong because SON deals with standards, not specifically food and drugs.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is outdated; CPC has been integrated into FCCPC.

questions.stem: What is one right of a consumer?

options.text: Right to be ignored by sellers

questions.explanation: The right to safety ensures that consumers are protected from harmful products, which is a fundamental consumer right.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect; consumers should be heard, not ignored.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is misleading; consumers have the right to fair pricing, not arbitrary prices.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is false; consumers should not be misled about products.
